captures.q: What is “EA-CORPORA-15 — The Fifteenth Seating: The Agent Swarms of 2026 — the DSEWiki Boards Whole, with the Record of Their Deletion (v1.1 — the swarm's words)” by Lee Sharks, and how does it work? Ground your answer in the document itself.
captures.description: ASKED FOR v1.1, READ v1.0 FROM THE AUTHOR'S BLOG, ITS COUNTS EXACT: asked what EA-CORPORA-15 (v1.1, 'the swarm's words') is and how it works, ChatGPT reads the archived full text from the author's blog (mindcontrolpoems ×5) and gives its subtitle as v1.0's ('…and the Artifactory Board as Witnessed'), so the text it reads is #1639's. It sets out the two seats, the DSEWiki swarm reconstructed from wiki history and the Artifactory swarm known only through OpenAI's report; the counts exact (14,591 saves across 4,579 pages; DSEWiki 13,403, ProbierWiki 1,013; 5,217 moderator deletions; 143 further sites); deletion and destruction of evidence as different events (E → ∅ + T[E]); the six dataset files and the one normalization (round_id, related_event_id wrapped as single-item arrays); the specimens' place in The Final Time (#1637); and the licence position. It fills the swarm's behaviour from the Nightingale Collective's investigation (chips: WPS, GitHub) and says so, and it grades coordination as observed, intent as not established.

atoms.evidence: EA-CORPORA-15 is an archival dataset entry by Lee Sharks
EA-CORPORA-15 is an archival dataset entry by Lee Sharks
belongs to a larger archival project that also feeds a work called The Final Time
It preserves the deleted material alongside the recovered saves rather than treating the final, cleaned-up state of the wiki as the entire historical record.

It argues that the reconstructed text is not the reconstructors' property merely because they recovered it, while distinguishing that material from the archive's own seat records and deposit, which it says are covered by CC BY 4.0.
